reflections.title: "If You Confess with Your Mouth"

reflect.text: Salvation is a rich word that means much more than escaping punishment for our wrong choices. As F. B. Meyer explains, it means being set free from the love and power of sin so that our hearts are made holy. God calls us to confess openly that Jesus is Lord. This means we willingly place Him on the throne of our lives, allowing Him to heal the deep roots of our sin like a wise doctor.

Along with our spoken words, we must believe with all our heart that God raised Jesus from the dead. Charles Spurgeon wrote that this promise is as "clear as the sun in the Heavens." When we place our sincere trust in the living Saviour, God guarantees our rescue. He delivers us from the guilt of sin today, sustains us with His risen life, and promises to bring us safely home at last.

questions: Have you openly confessed that Jesus is your Lord and King?
In what areas of your daily life do you need the living Christ to take control and heal you?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, we confess with our mouths that You are Lord of all. We believe with our whole hearts that God raised You from the dead to give us new life. Please rule over our thoughts and actions, and free us from the power of sin today. Amen.

reflections.title: "Faith Comes by Hearing"

reflect.text: Many people wonder how they can get more faith. Some try to produce faith out of wishful thinking, feelings, or guesswork, while others simply beg God to give them stronger belief. Yet Scripture tells us that faith is not a mystery we have to invent. Genuine faith arises naturally when we hear and take in the revealed truth of God.

God uses the message of Christ as His chosen tool to turn hearts toward Him. When we read or hear the good news of the cross, the Holy Spirit works through those words to clear away doubts and give us understanding. This truth not only brings new believers to salvation, but it also continually strengthens the confidence of those who already follow Jesus. When we rest on God's clear promises in the Bible, our trust becomes firm and steady.

questions: Do you rely on feelings for your faith, or do you root your trust in God's written promises?
How can spending more time listening to God's word help settle your doubts this week?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us Your truth in the Bible so our faith can grow. When doubts arise, help us look to Your promises rather than our own feelings. Send Your Holy Spirit to open our minds as we listen to the message of Christ. Amen.

D3.author: Adrian Rogers
D3.work: Stop Praying for Faith, Start Reading the Word

reflections.title: Sent to Share the Good News

reflect.text: In this passage, Paul challenges any attempt to earn God's approval through our own good deeds. Legalism, the false idea that keeping rules makes us right with God, only blinds us to our need for His grace. When we realize that righteousness comes through Christ alone, we are freed from trying to prove ourselves. Yet this freedom is not an invitation to hide away from those who do not know the Lord.

It is easy for Christians to pull back into comfortable bubbles where we only spend time with fellow believers. However, Jesus did the opposite by stepping directly into the brokenness of everyday people and pursuing those who were far from God. Men and women around us cannot call on a Saviour they have never heard about. To bring them the hope of the gospel, we must follow Christ's example, leave our comfort zones, and speak up with love.

questions: Have you settled into a comfortable bubble instead of reaching out to people who do not know Jesus?
Who is someone in your life who needs to hear the good news of Christ from you?
reflections.prayer: Lord, forgive us when we hide in our own comfort and forget the people around us. Give us the courage of Jesus to step into the lives of those who are hurting and searching. Help us to share Your good news with boldness and grace so others may hear and believe. Amen.
